topics.title: B. Associates Commercial Corp. v. Rash (1997) — Full Case and Dissent
topics.description: Supreme Court replacement-value standard, operative statutory sentences, footnote 6 and Stevens objection.

entries.title: Associates Commercial Corp. v. Rash, 520 U.S. 953 (1997)
entries.source: User-supplied casebook, Chapter 6 Secured Claims §B (Rash, §506(a)(2), original Problem 6.4); section locators not printed page estimates
entries.summary: Supreme Court reversed Fifth Circuit: Chapter13 retention cramdown requires replacement value—a willing buyer in debtor's circumstances pays for like property for proposed use—not expected foreclosure proceeds or midpoint. Remanded to determine factual replacement price.
entries.laymanExplanation: When debtor retains and uses collateral under Chapter13 cramdown, §506(a)(1)'s disposition/use directs replacement value, adjusted to property and debtor circumstances under Rash footnote 6 (subject to later §506(a)(2)).
entries.legalExplanation: Ginsburg explained §506(a)'s first sentence determines secured vs unsecured division and ownership/senior priority interests, not valuation method; second sentence expressly references purpose and proposed disposition/use. Retention yields economic value of keeping truck and differs from surrender; lender faces deferred payment risk/deterioration ('double risks'). Statute has no basis for mechanical average. Footnote 6 left room for whether replacement equals retail, wholesale or another figure based on property/debtor, excluding add-ons debtor doesn't receive, like warranties, inventory storage, reconditioning. Stevens dissent interpreted creditor's interest as what lender could realize on foreclosure and saw payment interest/adequate protection as risk protections.
entries.examApplication: Walk through $41,171 debt vs $31,875 foreclosure and ~$41k replacement; distinguish allowed secured amount, method, plan present value and market sale outcome.
entries.examTrap: Holding identifies replacement-standard, NOT blanket full retail price without adjustments.
entries.sourceRole: Full judicial opinion excerpted in uploaded Chapter 6
entries.facts: Elray Rash purchased 1989 Kenworth truck for freight business for $73,700 on installment secured by assigned lien to Associates Commercial (ACC). In March 1992 Elray and Jean Rash filed Chapter13; ACC loan balance $41,171. Debtors sought to keep truck and pay plan over 58 months using asserted $28,500 amount, later foreclosure appraisal expert $31,875; ACC wanted comparable-truck replacement estimated ~$41k. Bankruptcy/district courts and Fifth Circuit en banc used net foreclosure $31,875; Supreme Court reviewed split among circuits.
entries.issue: Under §506(a), when Chapter13 debtor keeps and uses business truck through cramdown §1325(a)(5)(B), should allowed secured claim use creditor's foreclosure recovery, debtor's replacement cost, or midpoint?
entries.holding: Supreme Court reversed Fifth Circuit: Chapter13 retention cramdown requires replacement value—a willing buyer in debtor's circumstances pays for like property for proposed use—not expected foreclosure proceeds or midpoint. Remanded to determine factual replacement price.
entries.reasoning: Ginsburg explained §506(a)'s first sentence determines secured vs unsecured division and ownership/senior priority interests, not valuation method; second sentence expressly references purpose and proposed disposition/use. Retention yields economic value of keeping truck and differs from surrender; lender faces deferred payment risk/deterioration ('double risks'). Statute has no basis for mechanical average. Footnote 6 left room for whether replacement equals retail, wholesale or another figure based on property/debtor, excluding add-ons debtor doesn't receive, like warranties, inventory storage, reconditioning. Stevens dissent interpreted creditor's interest as what lender could realize on foreclosure and saw payment interest/adequate protection as risk protections.
entries.rule: When debtor retains and uses collateral under Chapter13 cramdown, §506(a)(1)'s disposition/use directs replacement value, adjusted to property and debtor circumstances under Rash footnote 6 (subject to later §506(a)(2)).
entries.dissent: Justice Stevens: §506(a) focuses on creditor's interest; since cramdown is substitution for foreclosing, benchmark creditor's foreclosure proceeds. Interest payments and §361 adequate protection address risks, while larger replacement value is windfall to secured lender at unsecured creditors' expense.

entries.title: Majority first sentence answers extent, second sentence answers valuation method

entries.summary: §506(a) first sentence recognizes limited estate ownership and junior liens; second sentence tells court to value in light of purpose and actual use. Using foreclosure in retention would render second sentence ineffective.
entries.laymanExplanation: The first half tells what belongs to bank; the second tells price.
entries.legalExplanation: Statutory whole-text reading central to case.
entries.examApplication: For Professor question about 'creditor's interest', quote limited estate interest/senior lien examples.
entries.examTrap: Don't treat 'creditor's interest' as definition of foreclosure value.

entries.title: Rash footnote 6: replacement value need not be every retail component
entries.source: User-supplied casebook, Chapter 6 Secured Claims §B (Rash, §506(a)(2), original Problem 6.4); section locators not printed page estimates
entries.summary: Court let bankruptcy courts decide factually whether benchmark retail/wholesale/other; deduct amounts for warranties, inventory storage, reconditioning or upgrades not part of lien when buyer retains existing collateral.
entries.laymanExplanation: If you keep old truck, don't pay for a dealer's optional warranty you aren't receiving.
entries.legalExplanation: Source notes many courts used adjusted figure near midpoint after Rash; 2005 amendment later restricts this for individual Chapter7/13 consumer goods.
entries.examApplication: Specify nonreceived services and lien scope; don't count marketing deduct under subsequent §506(a)(2).

entries.title: Rash double risks and Stevens dissent
entries.source: User-supplied casebook, Chapter 6 Secured Claims §B (Rash, §506(a)(2), original Problem 6.4); section locators not printed page estimates
entries.summary: Majority: secured lender denied immediate sale and exposed to new default and depreciation by debtor's retained use; dissent: plan interest and adequate protection already compensate lender.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank worries car may be ruined before payments complete, but dissent says protections handle that.
entries.legalExplanation: This argument resurfaces Sunnyslope and Thomas concurrence in Till.
entries.examApplication: For compare quote rationale without claiming an absolute foreclosure-value floor.
entries.examTrap: Double risks language doesn't overrule explicit replacement/use instruction.

entries.title: Why simple midpoint rejected
entries.source: User-supplied casebook, Chapter 6 Secured Claims §B (Rash, §506(a)(2), original Problem 6.4); section locators not printed page estimates
entries.summary: §506(a) refers only to disposition/use actually proposed; mathematical average of hypothetical sale and retention scenarios is not grounded in text.
entries.laymanExplanation: Supreme Court wouldn't split a difference between two mutually exclusive scenarios.
entries.legalExplanation: Though bilateral monopoly bargaining may produce a settlement near midpoint, legal holding uses replacement.
entries.examApplication: Calculate midpoint separately only to illustrate rejected alternative.
entries.examTrap: Midpoint value can arise as factually supported replacement valuation, not court's required rule.

entries.laymanExplanation: Bank gets to vote yes, take car, or receive legally sufficient cash stream while debtor keeps it.
entries.legalExplanation: Retained car debtor must include time-value interest, addressed in Till.
entries.examApplication: In exam first select option A/B/C then valuation and interest.
entries.examTrap: Replacement amount and discount interest rate are different computations.

entries.summary: Second sentence §506(a)(2): individual Ch7/13 personal property acquired personal/family/household use uses price retail merchant would charge for that kind considering age/condition at time valued.

entries.legalExplanation: Book characterizes rule as largely foreclosing Rash footnote6 downward adjustments for consumer goods.
entries.examApplication: For Problem6.4 family SUV check §722 redemption or Ch13 treatment and 910 rule.
